The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The testOverrideVarianceWithMathClass test fails because it sets a custom variance implementation (Variance with isBiasCorrected set to false) in SummaryStatistics using setVarianceImpl. The test then adds values and checks that the variance computed by SummaryStatistics matches that computed directly by the Variance instance.

From the bug report and test, the issue is that after calling setVarianceImpl with a Statistics class like Variance, subsequent calls to getStandardDeviation produce NaN (not a number).

Looking at the implementation of setVarianceImpl in SummaryStatistics, it simply assigns the varianceImpl field to the new provided instance without resetting or reinitializing any internal counters like n that track how many samples have been added.

The getStandardDeviation method relies on getVariance, which calls varianceImpl.getResult(). The Variance stored in varianceImpl presumably computes variance incrementally using internally tracked state. However, setVarianceImpl is called after the internal sample count (e.g., n) has been set, but the new Variance instance is empty and has not seen any data. Therefore, varianceImpl.getResult() returns NaN because it has received no data points.

The addValue method of SummaryStatistics increments the internal statistics (sumImpl, minImpl, maxImpl, secondMoment) and also conditionally increments meanImpl, varianceImpl, and geoMeanImpl only if these are not instances of the default implementation types like Mean or Variance. Since we replaced varianceImpl with a new Variance instance just after initialization, addValue checks if varianceImpl is not instance of Variance and only then increments varianceImpl. But now varianceImpl actually is an instance of Variance, so the increment is not performed for the new instance. This causes the new varianceImpl instance to never receive any calls to increment upon addValue, so it remains empty.

Thus, the varianceImpl is never updated with sample values after being replaced, so getResult() returns NaN, and getStandardDeviation called on that variance returns NaN as well.

The root cause is that SummaryStatistics.addValue does not properly increment the varianceImpl when it has been replaced with a new Variance instance using setVarianceImpl, due to the logic that skips increment if varianceImpl "is instance of Variance" (i.e., the default implementation). After replacing the instance, the new varianceImpl should be incremented on addValue, but currently it is not.

Hence:
- setVarianceImpl replaces the varianceImpl with a new Variance object that has no data.
- addValue doesn't call increment on the replaced varianceImpl because it assumes default Variance impl is handled by secondMoment.
- varianceImpl remains empty, so getVariance returns NaN.
- getStandardDeviation uses getVariance and returns NaN.

This analysis explains the behavior observed in the test and the bug report.

Summary:
The bug occurs because SummaryStatistics.setVarianceImpl replaces varianceImpl, but addValue does not update the replaced varianceImpl instance properly, leading to NaN results when calling getStandardDeviation.

No recent bug reports relate to this specific issue.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
